newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch airlines to accept unlimited liability.
newsitem.headline: Dutch airlines to accept unlimited liability.

text.p: KLM, KLM Cityhopper, Martinair and Transavia will accept unlimited liability for accidents in which passengers are killed or injured, they said in a statement.
Earlier, the Financial Times reported European airlines KLM, SAS, Swissair, Austrian Airlines and Finnair will accept unlimited liability for such accidents.
The move will end the 1929 Warsaw Convention principle of limiting liability.
It pre-empts implementation next year of a deal negotiated by the International Air Transportation Association (IATA), dubbed the IATA Intercarrier Agreement, the paper said.
In 1983 KLM increased the limit for liability to around 250,000 guilders from around 40,000 guilders. This step was then followed by KLM Cityhopper, Martinair and Transavia, they said in a statement.
Martinair is jointly owned by KLM and Nedlloyd.
